page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.2xlarge is a graphics-intensive instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores, 2 threads per core) running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. Storage is provided via a 225 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a clear division between CPU-only tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU performance is generally modest, with single-core and multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores falling into the weak category. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are weak. However, memory bandwidth, PassMark CPU tests, and Redis SET operations perform at an average level. In contrast, the GPU-driven LLM inference benchmarks are highly competitive, achieving top-tier performance for prompt processing and strong performance for text generation on both small and medium models.

Given its hardware profile, the g4dn.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated computing. The inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU and local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and graphics-intensive tasks. However, the weaker single-core CPU performance represents a tradeoff, making it less optimal for CPU-bound sequential processing. It is best utilized for workloads that can offload computation to the GPU, such as model serving, video transcoding, and database operations that benefit from local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.2xlarge is a graphics-optimized instance designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, it features a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It also includes 225 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While CPU-only benchmarks, such as Geekbench and stress-ng, place the instance in the lower performance tiers, its GPU capabilities deliver top-tier results in LLM inference prompt processing and strong performance in text generation for small and medium models. This hardware configuration makes the instance a cost-effective choice for machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and video transcoding, though it presents a tradeoff for CPU-heavy sequential tasks.
